thesis: The speaker argues that the proliferation of venture capital funds has led to a market where many new investors lack experience and may mistakenly believe investing is easy, resulting in market distortions where less knowledgeable bidders win term sheets and pay too much. Additionally, the speaker suggests that the venture business model, which rewards a single major success with significant carried interest, may cause general partners to invest differently than if they were using their own money.
